title: Count the Number of Incremovable Subarrays I
summary: Given a 0-indexed array of positive integers, count the number of subarrays that, when removed, result in the remaining array being strictly increasing.
statement: Given a 0-indexed array of positive integers, count the number of subarrays that, when removed, result in the remaining array being strictly increasing. An empty array is considered strictly increasing. A subarray is a continuous segment of the original array.
constraints: The elements left behind must be strictly increasing; an empty or one-element remainder is increasing.
Return the number of removable subarrays satisfying that condition.
hints: The source-I constraints allow enumerating every removal interval.
Construct the prefix before left followed by the suffix after right.
Check strict increase across every adjacent pair of that remainder.
Every nonempty contiguous removal has a unique left/right pair, so the count is exhaustive and duplicate-free.
editorial: Every nonempty contiguous removal has a unique left/right pair, so the count is exhaustive and duplicate-free.

tests.explanation: Every one of the ten nonempty subarrays can be removed while leaving an increasing sequence.
Seven removal intervals leave a strictly increasing remainder.
